recipes.name: Layers Of Love Chocolate Brownies
ingredients_raw: 0.75 cup NESTLE® TOLL HOUSE® Baking Cocoa
0.75 cup NESTLE® TOLL HOUSE® Premier White Morsels
0.75 cup NESTLE® TOLL HOUSE® Semi-Sweet Chocolate Morsels

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Grease 8-inch-square baking pan.

Combine flour, cocoa and salt in small bowl. Beat butter, granulated sugar and brown sugar in large mixer bowl until creamy. Add 2 eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Add vanilla extract; mix well. Gradually beat in flour mixture. Reserve 3/4 cup batter. Spread remaining batter into prepared baking pan. Sprinkle nuts and white morsels over batter. Drizzle caramel topping over top. Beat remaining egg and reserved batter in same large bowl until light in color. Stir in semi-sweet morsels. Spread evenly over caramel topping.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes or until center is set. Cool completely in pan on wire rack. Cut into squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Layers Of Love Chocolate Brownies
raw_recipe.description: A finalist in the 2000 Share The Very Best Recipe Contest, this recipe was entered by Alma Carey of Sarasota, FL. Made with a genuine love of chocolate, this decadent brownie features vanilla-flavored white and semi-sweet chocolate morsels, chopped pecans and caramel layered within a rich cocoa batter.

review.reviewBody: I just made these after finding the original Nestle recipe in my recipe box...it's been there for about ten years, but I'd never made them. THEY ARE AMAZING homemade brownies. Had two requests for the recipe on my first debut :) Highly recommended to anyone looking for thick, fudgy delicious brownies that are not out of a box!

I am rating this a 5 star for the chocoholic in mind. For myself personally, they were very sweet and rich but they are decadent. I doubled the recipe using a 9x13 and baked a tad longer. They are rich, fudgy, and moist. The bottom layer batter will be very thick, as it has to hold the chips and caramel, and you don't want it to sink to the bottom. for doubling the recipe, I only used 1 cup each of the white chips and pecans. It was plenty. You will want to use a good caramel, and a thick one. I used Mrs. Richardson's which is very buttery and good. It is also very thick. I think if you were to use a thinner caramel, it would get lost. The Richardson's held a nice thickness. I used mini chips in the top portion of batter. I intend to cut these in smaller pieces, as they are very rich. The caramel middle looks very pretty and something different. I think this recipe could very easily stand on its own if one chose to fore go the caramel and white chips. I also made sure that I didn't spread the caramel too close to the sides, as I didn't want it to stick to the sides of the pan.

I loved this recipe! Made it for firefighters after a training and they loved it! I did leave out the nuts (for allergy reasons) and I threw the brownies in the fridge for about 2 hours after they cooled so they were hard enough to cut into individual bites. They were definitely a hit and I will be making this again!

Wow! I can end my brownie recipe search! I thought the batter was too thick too, but it worked out just fine. These are fudge, yet melt in your mouth good, and super rich. I used oil instead of butter, peanut butter sauce instead of caramel, extra-dark cocoa, and milk chocolate chips. You know they are done when they raise slightly and crack on the top.
I wanted to use a 13x9 pan so I doubled the recipe and it was fine. If I did it again I would decrease the caramel by 25% so the cake doesn't drip over. Every body totally loved these brownies.
Did not like this one, very dry, powdery texture
Why this recipe is five stars I don’t know. These were far from good brownies. While it had a brownie texture. They taste was off. They just were too sweet and likes chalky tasting.
was really hard to bake. not enough batter. maybe because we ate it all, yum!!!!!!
It was absolutely amazing its delicious.
I was so disappointed in this recipe! It was way too rich for my blood and too dense. I followed all the directions, so I don't think I messed anything up. Won't be making this again.
Everyone loved them. Cut them small because they are very sweet.

These were OK, but not sure I'd make them again. Too much going on in them that they lose definition--everything just tastes sweet. No chocolaty, just sweet. I think I'll just stick with nut in my brownies.
